completed_tasks.progress: Merged and gated. Followed by a large post-merge hardening pass this session (not a new wave -- infrastructure/quality work on top of wave 6): (1) found+fixed a real WCAG AA contrast bug across 3 color tokens (purple.300, red.500, red.300) beyond the one axe-core flagged; (2) found+fixed a real font-loading bug -- @storybook/nextjs-vite's next/font support resolves the import without erroring but produces no actual font files for a static `storybook build`, so typography tokens were silently falling back to the browser default in Storybook/Playwright (the real Next.js app was unaffected, since app/layout.tsx's next/font usage works correctly in a real `next build`) -- fixed by self-hosting the exact font files `next build` already fetches as plain static @font-face CSS (src/styles/fonts.css), which works identically everywhere without depending on Storybook's plugin; (3) chased a 'CI shows the wrong font' race across 7 CI round-trips (document.fonts.ready waits, requestAnimationFrame waits, font-display:block) before a rigorous zoomed-in pixel comparison against a known Arial reference showed the premise was likely a misjudgment from a non-zoomed glance at the very first screenshot -- reverted the speculative workarounds (font-display back to swap, dropped the extra wait logic), kept only the genuinely-needed self-hosted-font fix and a reasonable wait-for-story-content-before-screenshotting; (4) applied a user-requested code-quality batch: Props naming convention (ButtonProps/IconButtonProps -> plain Props, D-26w), Arrange/Act/Assert test markers on all existing tests (D-26x), documented the parametrized storyIds test-loop as a preferred pattern (D-26y), cropped visual-regression screenshots to actual story content instead of the full 1280x720 viewport (~97% smaller), moved 9 one-time pipeline artifacts out of repo root into docs/planning-history/, added a no-restricted-syntax ESLint rule banning inline `import("module").Type` type queries, removed an unused @testing-library/react dependency, and wrote a README.md documenting the full testing process. All work pushed to origin/master; CI green on every push.

decisions.decision: Component props types are named plainly `Props` (not `ButtonProps`/`IconButtonProps`) -- D-26w
decisions.rationale: No collision risk: each is scoped to its own module and never re-exported (D-26r, no barrel files). Applied retroactively to button.tsx/icon-button.tsx per explicit user sign-off.

decisions.decision: Tests follow Arrange/Act/Assert with explicit // Arrange / // Act / // Assert comments, even for one-line phases -- D-26x
decisions.rationale: User-requested convention, applied retroactively to all existing tests (button, icon-button, style-dictionary pipeline).

decisions.decision: Parametrized `for (const x of xs) { test(...) }` loops are the preferred (not mandatory) shape for a uniform family of test cases -- D-26y
decisions.rationale: User liked the storyIds loop in primitives.visual.spec.ts; documented as a pattern to reach for, not force.

decisions.decision: Font loading: self-host Plus Jakarta Sans via static @font-face (src/styles/fonts.css) instead of relying on next/font/google in each environment separately
decisions.rationale: next/font works correctly in the real Next.js app (next build genuinely fetches and self-hosts the font) but @storybook/nextjs-vite's next/font support does not produce real font files for a static `storybook build` -- confirmed by diffing storybook-static's output assets. A single static CSS source works identically everywhere without depending on that plugin's behavior.

decisions.decision: font-display: swap (not block) -- reverted after further investigation
decisions.rationale: block was adopted mid-session to defend against what looked like a CI-only font-rendering race across 7 round-trips of investigation; a rigorous zoomed pixel comparison against a known Arial reference showed the very first, unfixed CI baseline already matched the correct font, meaning the race likely never existed. Reverted to normal swap behavior (no invisible-text window on slow connections) and dropped the document.fonts.ready/double-rAF wait that was defending against it. Kept a plain wait for real story content to exist before screenshotting, as ordinary good practice independent of fonts.

decisions.decision: Visual-regression screenshots target the story's own root element at a 640x480 viewport, not the full page at Desktop Chrome's default 1280x720
decisions.rationale: Most primitives used under 10% of the default viewport -- wasted space in every baseline and every comparison. ~97% smaller baselines (single-button story: 1280x720 full-page -> ~125x40 cropped).

decisions.rationale: Historical record from the pre-project ideation pipeline, not living documents referenced during day-to-day development (unlike CONVENTIONS.md, which stays at root). User asked for root-level cleanup on a case-by-case basis.
